name: Zebu
notes:
Brought across the strait from Mainland Asia by people, and nowhere on Jambhudweep without them. Every zebu south of the Aravali is somebody's: it draws the ox cart, threshes by walking the floor in circles, gives milk morning and evening, and its dung is the fuel and the floor-plaster of every camp that has no wood. A loose one is a stray, and a stray is walked back.

The bull on the Harappan seals is this animal -- the hump, the dewlap, the heavy horns -- and the seals were cut by people who had been driving it for a thousand years. It is the one large mammal of the north that crossed, and it crossed because it was led. The wild things of Mainland Asia stayed on their shore; the ox came over on a rope.
journal_prompt: A humped ox tethered by a camp, chewing, with the look of an animal that has pulled a cart further than you have walked. Somebody's: there is a cord through its nose and a blue bead on its horn.
appearance: A lean, long-legged tawny ox with a low hump over the shoulders, a loose dewlap at the throat, large drooping ears and long upright horns ringed at the base. Dark hooves and a dark switch to the tail.
